initial_observation.encounter_context: Presented to the general practitioner with two days of fever, nausea, and vomiting without respiratory symptoms; then re-presented to the children's emergency
initial_observation.chief_complaint: acute dizziness, slurred speech, left gaze deviation, progressively unsteady gait, and subjective weakness
initial_observation.first_contact_summary: Presented initially with two days fever, nausea, and vomiting; SARS-CoV-2 antigen rapid test positive; discharged with symptomatic medications; returned next day with acute neurological symptoms; SARS-CoV-2 PCR positive with Ct 20.49; neurological exam showed reduced consciousness, expressive aphasia, bilateral partial ptosis with ophthalmoplegia and cerebellar signs
presenting_symptoms: bilateral cerebellar signs including dysdiadochokinesia and past-pointing
known_prior_history: partially vaccinated with one dose of tozinameran 100 μg (Pfizer-BioNTech) one month before infection

evidence_items.source_text: Neurological examination revealed reduced consciousness (Glasgow Coma Scale score of 12: E4V2M6), expressive aphasia, bilateral partial ptosis with ophthalmoplegia, bilateral cerebellar signs including dysdiadochokinesia, and past-pointing with mild truncal ataxia. He had normal tone and hyperreflexia in both knee and ankle jerks. Power was 5 (based on Medical Research Council grading) in both upper and lower limbs. His right eye was held in an adducted, downward gaze, whereas his left eye held a central, downward gaze, suggesting cranial nerves III and IV palsy, respectively.

Brain magnetic resonance imaging (Fig ) showed swelling and signal changes involving bilateral thalami, midbrain, pons, cerebellar hemispheres, and periventricular white matter, correlating with a diagnosis of ANEC.

Lumbar puncture revealed elevated CSF red cell count (25 cells/uL), elevated protein level (1.02 g/L), normal opening pressure, and no pleocytosis with normal glucose and lactate levels. Oligoclonal bands were absent. CSF meningoencephalitis infectious panel returned negative, including SARS-CoV-2 PCR.
Extensive serum and CSF autoimmune tests were negative, including anti-N-methyl-d-aspartate, anti-myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein, anti-glutamic-acid-decarboxylase, and anti-GQ1b-ganglioside IgG.
Inflammatory markers were elevated: erythrocyte sedimentation rate 65 mm/hr, C-reactive-protein 36 mg/L, and procalcitonin 12.1 μg/L. However, ferritin levels and liver function tests were normal.
Given these results, his ANEC Severity Score was 5 of 9, conferring high-risk for poor neurological outcome.

The patient was promptly initiated on immunotherapy with intravenous (IV) methylprednisolone 1000 mg daily for 5 days and intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) 2 g/kg over two days. He also received one dose of IV tocilizumab 8 mg/kg 12 hours from hospital presentation. Normothermia at 35°C to 36°C was maintained for six days. Serum sodium levels were kept minimally at 140 mmol/L for neuroprotection. He received a five-day course of IV remdesivir to treat SARS-CoV-2. Other concurrent antimicrobials included empirical IV ceftriaxone, azithromycin, acyclovir, and oseltamivir, until respective viral and bacterial studies returned negative.

After eight days, he demonstrated good response to treatment; Glasgow Coma Scale improved to 15, ophthalmoplegia and ataxia improved, and mRS score reduced to 2. He was discharged home after 16 days with residual deficits including mild ophthalmoplegia, upper limb dysmetria with intention tremor, mild aphasia, and dysarthria. At discharge, mRS score was 1. Two weeks later, mRS score improved to 0, indicating neurological function recovery.

Unenhanced computed tomography brain hypodensity in the bilateral thalami (A, top left image) and cerebellar hemispheres (not shown). Contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) showed restricted diffusion in the thalami. (B, top right image) Postcontrast enhancement MRI shows swelling and increased T2-weighted signal with postcontrast peripheral rim enhancement in cerebellar hemispheres. (C, bottom left image) Presence of susceptibility artifact over the brainstem and cerebellar hemispheres (D, bottom right image) in keeping with blood products in the same regions.

Diagnostic considerations included SARS-CoV-2-associated ANEC, ADEM, acute brainstem encephalitis, and Miller Fisher syndrome.
Lumbar puncture revealed elevated CSF red cell count (25 cells/uL), elevated protein level (1.02 g/L), normal opening pressure, and no pleocytosis with normal glucose and lactate levels.
Extensive serum and CSF autoimmune tests were negative, including anti-N-methyl-d-aspartate, anti-myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein, anti-glutamic-acid-decarboxylase, and anti-GQ1b-ganglioside IgG.
